mechanic: One reasoning move: a thing was in one state and then in another, so someone changed it between; the act that changes it has needs (a key, being at the door), and each suspect is set against them.
note: Spoilers. The logic written before the prose, in the shape sketched in docs/archipelago-plan.md. `frame` is what the narrator's own prose always carries; `clues` are the units that could be case files. `facts` names the world model's facts that realise a clue, `chain` the tellings that bring it.

frame.says: The cellar door was locked at ten on Friday night and stood open at six on Saturday morning, the brandy cask a gallon lighter.
Two men about the place might have done it: the ostler and the potman.

questions.asks: Who opened the cellar door in the night?

rules_out.Ned Sharp: c.keys: he has no key; c.loft: he was across the yard all night
rules_out.the narrator: her own word only: she holds the other key and tells the story

clues.says: The ostler was dead drunk in the yard; the potman was sober.

clues.source: The narrator's own knowledge of her house
clues.says: The cellar door opens off the passage; it has two keys, hers and the one the potman carries night and day.

clues.source: The carrier's man, to the narrator: his night in the stable loft
clues.says: The ostler was up in the loft before ten and never stirred till six.
clues.note: The witness turns out to be the buyer of the brandy; what he says of the ostler is true.

clues.source: The narrator's own knowledge of her house
clues.says: The potman sleeps on the settle in the passage, from ten until six.
